questions.question: At which OSI layer are bits represented as electrical, radio or optical signals?
questions.explanation: The physical layer defines transmission over the medium.

option_explanations.A: The physical layer defines transmission over the medium.
option_explanations.B: Network handles logical addressing and routing.
option_explanations.D: Data Link organizes bits into frames and mediates local delivery.

questions.question: Which OSI layer handles Ethernet frame delivery on a local link?
questions.explanation: Ethernet framing and MAC addressing are data-link functions.

option_explanations.D: Ethernet framing and MAC addressing are data-link functions.

questions.question: A laptop moves to a different subnet and receives a new IPv4 address while retaining its Ethernet MAC. Which layer owns the changed address?
questions.explanation: The IPv4 address belongs to Layer 3. The Ethernet MAC belongs to Layer 2.

option_explanations.B: The unchanged MAC belongs to the data-link layer.
option_explanations.C: The IPv4 address belongs to Layer 3. The Ethernet MAC belongs to Layer 2.

questions.question: What is the conventional name of the transport-layer PDU for TCP?
questions.explanation: TCP encapsulates bytes in segments, which IP then carries in packets.

option_explanations.B: TCP encapsulates bytes in segments, which IP then carries in packets.
option_explanations.C: An Ethernet header belongs to the link layer.
option_explanations.D: A frame is the data-link PDU.

questions.question: Which ordering starts immediately above OSI transport and moves upward?
questions.explanation: The layers above transport are session (5), presentation (6) and application (7).

option_explanations.A: The layers above transport are session (5), presentation (6) and application (7).
option_explanations.C: This is the descending order rather than the ascending order.
option_explanations.D: Data Link and Network are below Transport.

questions.question: Which OSI layers are broadly grouped into the TCP/IP application layer?
questions.explanation: TCP/IP groups these upper-layer functions into its application layer.

option_explanations.A: Physical and Data Link are grouped at the link or network-access level.
option_explanations.B: TCP/IP groups these upper-layer functions into its application layer.
option_explanations.C: Data Link and Network are not bundled with the TCP/IP application layer.
option_explanations.D: Network and Transport are distinct lower layers in that model.

questions.question: How is a TCP segment carried across an IPv4 Ethernet link?

options.A: The segment and IP packet are separate Ethernet headers
options.B: The IP packet is inside a TCP segment inside a frame
options.C: The segment is inside an IP packet inside an Ethernet frame
options.D: The Ethernet frame is inside a TCP segment inside an IP packet

questions.explanation: IP carries the segment and Ethernet carries the resulting IP packet.

option_explanations.A: The headers are nested payloads, not separate Ethernet headers.
option_explanations.B: IP wraps TCP rather than TCP wrapping IP.
option_explanations.C: IP carries the segment and Ethernet carries the resulting IP packet.
option_explanations.D: The Ethernet frame is the outer unit on the link.

questions.question: After a host accepts an Ethernet frame carrying IPv4, which information identifies TCP as the next protocol?
questions.explanation: EtherType identifies IPv4, then the IPv4 Protocol field identifies its payload as TCP.

option_explanations.B: EtherType identifies IPv4, then the IPv4 Protocol field identifies its payload as TCP.
option_explanations.C: TCP's window is available only after TCP is identified and parsed.
option_explanations.D: The MAC identifies the Ethernet sender, not the IP payload protocol.

questions.question: A router forwards an IPv4 packet between Ethernet links without NAT. Which field ordinarily changes to name the next hop on the second link?
questions.explanation: The router builds a fresh link-layer frame appropriate for the outgoing link.

option_explanations.A: The original IPv4 destination remains end-to-end without NAT.
option_explanations.B: The TCP destination port names the original application endpoint.
option_explanations.C: The router builds a fresh link-layer frame appropriate for the outgoing link.
option_explanations.D: The ACK number is part of the end-to-end TCP conversation.

questions.question: A client receives a valid Ethernet frame and its IPv4 payload, but a TCP connection attempt to the listed port receives a reset. Which layer reports the reset?
questions.explanation: TCP flags, including RST, are interpreted at the transport layer even when lower-layer delivery succeeds.

option_explanations.A: IP delivers the packet but has no TCP reset flag.
option_explanations.B: Presentation concerns representation rather than connection flags.
option_explanations.C: Ethernet carries the reset packet but does not generate the TCP RST indication.
option_explanations.D: TCP flags, including RST, are interpreted at the transport layer even when lower-layer delivery succeeds.
